report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of mutate.py: generate() claims deterministic generation, no-go filters, and inspectable rejection tallies; verified against code.

handoff.purpose: Verify generate()'s docstring/comment claims against the implementation in this chunk.

symbols.name: OPERATORS
symbols.note: Tuple of five mutation operator constants.

symbols.name: OPERATOR_CLASS
symbols.note: Maps each operator to a defect class string.

symbols.name: generate
symbols.note: Top-level mutant generator; deterministic via seed; collects sites, filters, mutates, and returns Mutant list.

claims.text: Generate ``count`` parseable mutants over real functions. Deterministic.
claims.why: Uses random.Random(seed) for deterministic randomness; parseable enforced by ast.parse(mutated) check; real functions from repo files.

claims.text: a big file cannot dominate merely by being walked first.
claims.why: Sites are collected from all files first, then rng.shuffle(sites) randomizes order, so file order does not dominate selection.

claims.text: Reported rather than discarded, because a filter nobody can see the effect of is the same shape of defect as a filter nobody calls
claims.why: filtered dict is populated via _refuse and later published as generate.last_filtered.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: these filters were defined, documented as built, and CALLED FROM NOWHERE. Every one of SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block and covered_lines appeared exactly once in this file -- its own definition.
claims.why: This chunk shows SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _in_main_block, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, covered_lines are used in this chunk (e.g., _in_main_block called on line ~337, SKIP_PATH_PARTS on line ~324, SKIP_FUNCTIONS on line ~330), but the claim about their definitions appearing exactly once reaches beyond this chunk.

claims.text: The corpus behind the published 75.3% detection figure was therefore minted without any of them, including on __repr__ bodies and log strings, which is precisely what they exist to exclude.
claims.why: The 75.3% figure and the historical claim about the corpus are not verifiable from this chunk; the filters are present and called here.

claims.text: a syntax error is a typo, not a defect
claims.why: Code checks ast.parse(mutated) and skips on SyntaxError, treating them as not defects.

claims.text: Undetectable by construction. Keeping it would depress every score measured against this corpus for a reason that is not the detector's fault, which is exactly how a metric starts lying.
claims.why: Code checks trivially_equivalent(original, mutated) and skips those mutants, with rationale matching the comment.
generate.last_rejected is set to dict(sorted(rejected.items())), making it inspectable.

claims.text: Published for the same reason as ``last_rejected``: a filter whose effect nobody can observe is one refactor away from being a filter nobody calls, which is exactly the state these were found in.
claims.why: generate.last_filtered is set to dict(sorted(filtered.items())), making it inspectable.
Uses random.Random(seed) for all randomness; no other nondeterministic sources in this chunk.

observations.what: generate.last_rejected and generate.last_filtered are set as attributes on the function object after return; this is a side effect that persists across calls.

The 'filtered' dict is only updated via _refuse for SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, and _in_main_block; other filters mentioned in comments (_is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, covered_lines) are not called in this chunk, so their effect on filtering is not observable here.

The mutation operators DROP_CALL, EARLY_RETURN, INVERT_CONDITION, WEAKEN_COMPARISON, CHANGE_CONSTANT, DROP_ARGUMENT are defined in the first part of the file; this chunk's generate() uses them via OPERATORS and OPERATOR_CLASS.

The claim about 'CALLED FROM NOWHERE' is contradicted by this chunk for _in_main_block (called on line ~337) and SKIP_PATH_PARTS/SKIP_FUNCTIONS (used on lines ~324 and ~330), but the overall claim about definitions appearing once is uncheckable.
